name: Barabati Fort
century: 14th Century CE (Ganga & Gajapati Dynasties, King Mukundadeva)
category: Medieval Riverine Fortress & Nine-Storey Palace Mound
description: Monumental arched laterite stone gateway, defensive moat ramparts, ancient stone bastion towers, and the historic nine-storey palace mound on the banks of Mahanadi.

hotspots.title: Pointed Arch Stone Gateway
hotspots.description: Impressive laterite stone gateway featuring a pointed Indo-Islamic influenced arched portal flanked by octagonal bastion guard towers.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Sole surviving monumental gateway of the 14th-century capital citadel of Kataka Barabati.

hotspots.title: Nine-Storey Palace Mound (Nava-Tala)
hotspots.description: Centrally located elevated mound where excavations revealed the structural stone column bases and courtyard of King Mukundadeva's palace.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Documented by Mughal and European travelers as one of the most imposing palace strongholds in eastern India.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India Excavation Branch & Cuttack Heritage Circle
sources.source: Excavation Reports at Barabati Fort Citadel
sources.attribution: ASI Bhubaneswar Circle & Govt. of Odisha

reconstruction_notes: Photogrammetric surface reconstruction of the surviving 14th-century pointed arch entrance gate in progress. Verified medieval bastion and fortress moat spatial reference enabled.
surrounding_environment: Mahanadi river delta plains, historic Cuttack city moat, and lush manicured citadel grounds
